metadata.description: Merged real benchmark results from 3 Ollama cloud models

gemma4:31b-cloud.notes: Extreme frequency bias toward ChaCha20 when blind

gpt-oss:120b-cloud.blind_bias: AES-256 (43% of blind guesses) + structural awareness
gpt-oss:120b-cloud.notes: Shows some discrimination for RSA and KEM, but hallucinates AES-256

nemotron-3-super:cloud.notes: Best blind performer; correctly identifies DES, RSA, KEM structure

key_findings: All models achieve 100% accuracy with full metadata (Tier-1)
Average blind accuracy (Tier-3) is only 38.1%, confirming metadata-dependence
Maximum metadata gap observed: 85.7 percentage points (gemma4)
Minimum metadata gap observed: 42.9 percentage points (nemotron)
Model-specific frequency biases vary: ChaCha20 (gemma4), AES-256 (gpt-oss), balanced (nemotron)
Structurally distinct ciphers (RSA-2048, ML-KEM-768) are correctly identified by all models even in blind mode
Symmetric stream block ciphers (AES, ChaCha20, 3DES) are consistently confused when metadata is removed
implications_for_revision: Empirically validates the 'metadata gap' thesis across 3 independent models
Confirms that 'expert-level cryptanalysis' claims are unsupported; best blind accuracy is 57.1%
Shows prompt engineering with statistical features is insufficient to close the gap
Larger model size does not guarantee better blind performance (120B gpt-oss vs unknown nemotron)
Provides a reproducible benchmark protocol that can be extended to 140+ samples
